## Model Predictions by PID & Distribution Train {height="50%"}
```{python}
#| title: "RMSE Comparison"
#| width: 40%

from IPython.display import Markdown, display

rmse_table = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "Model RMSE": [lasso_est, ridge_est, net_est],
        "Kaggle RMSE": [0.15410, 0.14920, 0.14912],
    },
    index=["Lasso", "Ridge", "Elastic Net"],
)

rmse_table

rmse_long = (
    rmse_table
    .reset_index()
    .rename(columns={"index": "Model"})
    .melt(id_vars="Model", var_name="Source", value_name="RMSE")
)

rmse_long["Model"] = pd.Categorical(
    rmse_long["Model"],
    categories=["Lasso", "Elastic Net", "Ridge"],
    ordered=True,
)

# Text about the metric
display(
    Markdown(
        "RMSE is computed on the log of SalePrice."
    )
)

# Text about Elastic Net being best
display(
    Markdown(
        "**Elastic Net achieves the lowest RMSE and its Kaggle RMSE is close to its "
        "internal RMSE, indicating good generalization compared with Ridge and Lasso.**"
    )
)

# Numeric performance summary
net_kaggle_rmse = 0.14912
net_gap = abs(net_est - net_kaggle_rmse)
net_vs_lasso = (lasso_est - net_est) / lasso_est * 100

display(
    Markdown(
        "**Performance Summary**  \n"
        f"- Elastic Net RMSE: `{net_est:.5f}` (Kaggle: `{net_kaggle_rmse:.5f}`)  \n"
        f"- Gap between internal and Kaggle RMSE: `{net_gap:.5f}`  \n"
        f"- Improvement vs Lasso: **{net_vs_lasso:.1f}%** lower RMSE."
    )
)
```

```{python}
#| title: "Training SalePrice Distribution"

saleprice_df = pd.DataFrame({"SalePrice": train["SalePrice"]})

(
    ggplot(saleprice_df, aes(x="SalePrice"))
    + geom_histogram(bins=30, color="black", alpha=0.6)
    + labs(
        title="Training SalePrice Distribution",
        x="SalePrice",
        y="Count",
    )
    + theme_minimal()
    + theme(figure_size=(8, 4))
)
```

## Prediction Distribution {height="50%"}

```{python}

#| title: "Model Predictions by Model"
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6
#| width: 40%


dist_df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "Elastic Net": y_pred,
        "Lasso": y_pred2,
        "Ridge": y_pred3
    }
)

dist_long = dist_df.melt(var_name="Model", value_name="Prediction")

ggplot(dist_long, aes(x="Model", y="Prediction", fill="Model")) + \
    geom_boxplot() + \
    scale_fill_manual(
        values={
            "Elastic Net": "red",
            "Lasso": "blue",
            "Ridge": "green"
        }
    ) + \
    labs(
        title="Prediction Boxplot by Model",
        x="Model",
        y="Predicted Value",
        fill="Model"
    )
```

```{python}
#| title: "Elastic Net Predictions Are Less Right-Skewed Than Training Prices”"
#| fig-cap: Elastic Net achieves lowest RMSE and prediction distribution less right-skewed than training SalePrice values indicating better overall performance and more stable predictions.

dist_df = pd.DataFrame({"y_pred": y_pred})

(
    ggplot(dist_df, aes(x="y_pred"))
    + geom_histogram(bins=30, color="black", alpha=0.6)
    + labs(
        title="Elastic Net Prediction Distribution",
        x="y_pred",
        y="Count",
    ) 
    + theme_minimal()
    + theme(figure_size=(8, 3))  
)

```
